title: Chat UI is a System
summary: This lesson breaks down six critical design decisions for building a professional chat interface. It focuses on reducing visual noise through message grouping, optimistic UI states, and smart scroll anchoring.

transcript.text: Chat UI is a system. Six decisions, same thread, half the noise.
Same sender, under two minutes, one group, one avatar. 4 pixel gap inside, 16 between groups. The reader scans people, not lines.
No time on every bubble. A date divider when the date changes. The exact time only on hover. Precision on demand, never in the way.
Hit enter, the bubble is there. Sent state fades in after. Failed shows a red retry, inline, on the message. Never a spinner between you and your own words.
New message while you read? The list does not jump, a pill counts them. Tap it, you slide to the bottom. Anchoring only when you are already there.
The typing indicator lives in the flow, where the next message lands. Three dots, avatar attached. It leaves without moving anything else.
The composer grows to five lines then scrolls. Enter sends, shift-enter breaks. Attachments preview above the text, never inside.
Six decisions. One thread that reads. Now make Claude code think like a senior UX designer.

on_screen_text: Think like a senior UX designer
design_principles: Reduce visual noise by grouping messages from the same sender within a 2-minute window.
Use proximity (4px vs 16px) to define relationships between message bubbles.
Progressive disclosure: show exact timestamps only on hover to keep the UI clean.
Optimistic UI: show the message bubble immediately upon sending to improve perceived performance.
Avoid layout shifts: use scroll anchoring to prevent the list from jumping when new messages arrive.
Contextual placement: place typing indicators exactly where the next message will appear.
before_after: A chat thread with 13 redundant avatars is transformed into a streamlined thread with only 7 avatars using smart grouping logic.
